draft.title: Wellbeing within India
card: Wellbeing can differ a lot inside one country. India is a clear case, because average figures hide big gaps between places.
Cities such as Mumbai tend to have higher incomes, more jobs and more hospitals and schools than many rural areas.
Many poorer rural areas, such as parts of Rajasthan, tend to have lower incomes and fewer services. Farming work can be uncertain and services can be far away.
Cities have gaps too. Some people in Mumbai live in crowded informal settlements with poor services, so wellbeing varies within a place as well as between places.
draft.remember: Wellbeing in India varies widely, between regions and within them.

a.q: Why does India's national average wellbeing figure give a poor picture of life there?
opts: It hides large differences between places and groups
It only counts people who live in the largest cities
It measures income but ignores every service
It is the same for every state, so it shows no change
a.why: A single national figure blends high and low results together. Wellbeing in India differs between cities and rural areas, and within cities too. The figure does not only count city people.
a.clue: Think about what an average does to very high and very low results.

b.q: Asha says all people in Mumbai have high wellbeing because it is a wealthy city. What is the best reply?
opts: Some Mumbai people live in crowded, poorly served areas
Mumbai has fewer jobs and schools than rural Rajasthan
Wellbeing in India is the same in every city and village
Only rural areas of India have people with low incomes
b.why: Cities tend to have higher incomes and more services, but not everyone shares them. Some people in Mumbai live in informal settlements with poor services. Saying Mumbai has fewer jobs and schools than rural areas reverses the general pattern.
b.clue: A place with higher wellbeing overall can still have people left behind.

a.best: It hides large differences between places and groups

b.best: Some Mumbai people live in crowded, poorly served areas
